1.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [6:1](ta:06).
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:16.

2.note: See how you translated **Son of man** in [2:1](ta:02).
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:11.

2.q: וְ⁠אָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֔ם אֶ֕רֶץ כִּֽי אָבִ֥יא עָלֶ֖י⁠הָ חָ֑רֶב
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and tell them that when I bring a sword against a land]

Here, **a sword** represents “an enemy army” that attacks with swords. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [When I bring an enemy army against a land]

Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that he might bring war against a land and the people of that land might choose one of their men to be a watchman. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [If]

3.note: A **shofar** is a kind of trumpet made from the horn of a ram. If your readers would not be familiar with what a shofar is, you could use the name of a similar thing that your readers would recognize, or you could use a more general term. Alternate translation: [and blows on the trumpet]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:17.

4.note: The expression **is not warned** is a passive verbal form. Here it means that the person does not pay attention to the warning. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and does not heed the warning]

Yahweh is speaking of **a sword** as if it were a living thing that could come and take a person away. He means that enemy soldiers with swords come and kill the person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and enemies with swords attack and kill him]

Yahweh is using **his blood will be on his head** as a common expression of the culture to mean “he will be responsible for his own death.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he alone will be to blame for his death]

5.note: See how you translated this phrase in 33:4.

The expression **being warned** is a passive verbal form. Here it means that the person pays attention to the warning. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [But if he heeds the warning]

6.note: The expression **are not warned** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who would do the action, it is the watchman. Alternate translation: [and he does not warn the people]
The pronoun **he** refers to the person whom the enemy kills, not to the watchman. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [that person is taken in his iniquity]

The expression **he is taken** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who would do the action, it is the enemy who comes with the sword. Alternate translation: [he dies by the enemy’s sword in his iniquity]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **iniquity**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [because of the evil things he has done]

Yahweh is using **his blood I will demand from the hand of the watchman** as a common expression of the culture to mean “I will hold the watchman responsible for that person’s death.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [but I will punish the watchman for that person’s death]
See how you translated the similar expression in 33:3.
See how you translated the similar expression in 33:4.

7.note: See how you translated this expression in 3:17.
See how you translated this phrase in [3:1](ta:03).

Here, **my mouth** represents “what I say.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [And you will hear a word that I speak]
See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:17.
See how you translated the similar expression in [4:1](ta:04).

8.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [When I tell the wicked one that he will surely die]

Yahweh is using the adjective **wicked** as a noun to mean a certain kind of person. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this adjective with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [When I say to a person who does evil]

Yahweh is repeating forms of the verb **die** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [you will surely die]

Yahweh is speaking of how a wicked person behaves as if it were a **way** or path on which he walks. He means that Ezekiel should warn the wicked person to stop behaving wickedly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to warn the wicked one to stop his wicked conduct]

9.note: Yahweh is speaking of stopping evil behavior as if it were to **turn back** from a path. He means that the wicked person would stop behaving wickedly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [so that he will stop doing it]
See how you translated the similar expression in 33:8.
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:19.

10.q: אֱמֹר֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֵּ֤ן אֲמַרְתֶּם֙ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר כִּֽי פְשָׁעֵ֥י⁠נוּ וְ⁠חַטֹּאתֵ֖י⁠נוּ עָלֵ֑י⁠נוּ
10.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [say to the house of Israel that they have been saying, “Surely our transgressions and our sins are upon us]

The Israelites are speaking of **our transgressions and our sins** as if they were heavy loads that were **upon us**. They mean that they feel guilty and are suffering the punishment for what they did. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [we are guilty of our transgressions and our sins and are suffering punishment for them]

The terms **transgressions** and **sins** mean similar things. The Israelites are using the two terms together for emphasis. If it would be clearer for your readers, you could express the emphasis with a single phrase. Alternate translation: [our many sins]

The Israelites are speaking of themselves as if they were something that is **rotting away**. They mean that they are becoming weaker and weaker because of their sins and the punishment for them. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and because of them we are becoming weaker and weaker]

The Israelites are using the question form for emphasis, to express that they have no hope of continuing to live. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And there is no way for us to go on living!”]
See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).

11.q: חַי אָ֣נִי נְאֻ֣ם אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהוִ֗ה אִם אֶחְפֹּץ֙
11.note: Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by his own life, and he is stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). The implied meaning is that he certainly does not **delight in the death of the wicked one**. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [As surely as I live’—the declaration of the Lord Yahweh—‘I certainly do not delight]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:11.
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **death**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [in it when the wicked one dies]

Yahweh is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [but rather I delight in the turning back]

Yahweh is repeating the verb **Turn back** in order to intensify his expression of the idea that it conveys. If your language can repeat words for intensification, it would be appropriate to do that here in your translation. If not, your language may have another way of expressing the intensification. Alternate translation: [Turn back completely from your evil ways]

Yahweh is using the question form to urge the Israelites to repent so that they will not die. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [And there is no reason for you to die, house of Israel!]
See how you translated the similar expression in 20:44.

12.note: Yahweh is speaking of **righteousness** as if it were a living thing that could **deliver** a person. He means that the right things a righteous person did before will not keep him from being punished if he later sins. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The righteous one will not escape punishment because of the right things he did]

Yahweh is using **in the day of his transgression** as a common expression of the culture to mean “when he transgresses.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when he transgresses]

If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about the wicked person not stumbling before the information about **the wickedness of the wicked**. Alternate translation: [and the wicked one will not stumble by his wickedness]

Yahweh is speaking of being ruined or punished as if it were to **stumble**. He means that the wicked person will not be punished because of the wicked things he did before. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he will not be punished because of it]

The pronoun **it** refers to the righteousness of the righteous person, that is, the right things that he did before. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to live by his past righteousness]
See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).

13.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 3:21.

The expression **will not be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who would do the action, it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [I will not remember any of his righteousness]

Yahweh is using **will not be remembered** as a common expression of the culture to mean “will not be taken into account.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [none of his righteousness will be taken into account]

14.note: If your language does not use nouns for the ideas of **justice** and **righteousness**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [and acts in ways that are just and right]
See how you translated the similar expression in 33:8.

15.note: The implication is that the **pledge** is an object that a borrower gave to the wicked person as a guarantee that he would repay a loan, and that the wicked person now gives it back. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the wicked returns to a borrower the object he took to guarantee a loan]

Yahweh is speaking of obeying his laws as if it were walking on a path. When he says that the person **walks in the statutes of life**, he means that the person obeys the laws that lead to life. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he obeys the statutes that give life]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:21.

16.q: כָּל חטאת⁠ו אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָטָ֔א לֹ֥א תִזָּכַ֖רְנָה ל֑⁠וֹ
16.note: The expression **will not be remembered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who would do the action, it is Yahweh. Alternate translation: [I will not remember against him any of the sin that he sinned]

Yahweh is using a construction in which a verb and its object come from the same root. You may be able to use the same construction in your language to express the meaning here. Alternatively, your language may have another way of saying this.
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:21.

17.note: The Israelites are speaking of how the Lord acts as if it were a **way** or path on which he walks. They mean that they think the Lord does not act fairly. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [The Lord does not act fairly]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:11.

18.note: The pronoun **them** refers to the unjust things that the righteous person does. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [then he will die in those unjust deeds]

19.q: וּ⁠בְ⁠שׁ֤וּב רָשָׁע֙ מֵֽ⁠רִשְׁעָת֔⁠וֹ וְ⁠עָשָׂ֥ה מִשְׁפָּ֖ט וּ⁠צְדָקָ֑ה
19.note: Yahweh is presenting a possible condition, that a wicked person might turn back from his wickedness and do what is just and right. Use a natural form in your language for introducing a condition that could happen. Alternate translation: [And if a wicked person turns back from his wickedness and does justice and righteousness]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **wickedness**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [from doing what is wicked]
See how you translated the similar expression in 33:14.

Yahweh is stating the pronoun **he** separately, even though the verb translated as **will live** already includes this meaning. He is doing that to emphasize that the person who turns back from his wickedness will surely live. If a speaker of your language would use an explicit pronoun for the same purpose, you may want to use that construction in your translation. If not, your language may have other ways of showing the meaning here. Alternate translation: [he himself will live]

20.q: אִ֧ישׁ כִּ⁠דְרָכָ֛י⁠ו אֶשְׁפּ֥וֹט אֶתְ⁠כֶ֖ם בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
20.note: This is the end of what Yahweh told Ezekiel to say to the Israelites, which began in verse 12, and the end of what Yahweh said to Ezekiel, which began in verse 2. You may wish to mark the end of these quotations with closing quotation marks or with some other punctuation or convention that your language uses to indicate the end of a quotation.

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means each person among the Israelites. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [I will judge each one of you according to his own ways]
See how you translated the similar expression in [3:1](ta:03).

21.note: Ezekiel is using the phrase translated as **Now it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

If your language would not represent a number in a form such as **twelfth**, you could represent this number in a form that your language would use. Alternate translation: [in year twelve of our exile]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **exile**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [since we had been taken away from our land]

The expression **has been struck** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was the Babylonian army. Alternate translation: [The Babylonian army has struck the city]

The implication is that the Babylonian army had attacked and captured Jerusalem. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The Babylonian army has attacked and captured the city]

The **tenth** month of the Hebrew calendar includes parts of December and January on Western calendars. You could convert the Hebrew day and month into an approximate date on the calendar that your culture uses. However, the Jews used a lunar calendar, so if you use a solar calendar, the date will be different every year, and the translation will not be entirely accurate. So you may just want to give the number of the day and the name of the month on the Hebrew calendar and say in a footnote approximately what time of year that is on your calendar.

22.note: Ezekiel is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

Here, **the hand** represents “the power.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [Now the power of Yahweh was upon me]

Ezekiel is using **to the face of the coming of the fugitive** as a common expression of the culture to mean “before the fugitive arrived.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [before the fugitive arrived]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:27.

The expression **my mouth was opened** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, it was Yahweh. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh opened my mouth]

23.note: See how you translated the similar expression in [6:1](ta:06).

24.q: יֹ֠שְׁבֵי הֶ⁠חֳרָב֨וֹת הָ⁠אֵ֜לֶּה עַל אַדְמַ֤ת יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֹמְרִ֣ים לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר אֶחָד֙ הָיָ֣ה אַבְרָהָ֔ם וַ⁠יִּירַ֖שׁ אֶת הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ
24.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [the dwellers of these ruins on the land of Israel keep saying that Abraham was only one man and he possessed the land, but they are many, so the land has been given to them as a possession]
The term **saying** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly.

24.q: אֶחָד֙ הָיָ֣ה אַבְרָהָ֔ם וַ⁠יִּירַ֖שׁ אֶת הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ וַ⁠אֲנַ֣חְנוּ רַבִּ֔ים לָ֛⁠נוּ נִתְּנָ֥ה הָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ לְ⁠מוֹרָשָֽׁה
24.note: The implication is that if Yahweh gave the land to Abraham even though he was only one man, he would certainly give it to them, since there are many of them. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [Abraham was only one man, and he possessed the land, but we are many; so surely the land has been given to us as a possession]

The expression **has been given** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. If you must state who did the action, the people mean that Yahweh has given them the land. Alternate translation: [Yahweh has given the land to us as a possession]
If your language does not use a noun for the idea of **possession**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [for us to own]
See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).

25.q: לָ⁠כֵן֩ אֱמֹ֨ר אֲלֵי⁠הֶ֜ם כֹּֽה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣⁠י יְהֹוִ֗ה עַל הַ⁠דָּ֧ם תֹּאכֵ֛לוּ
25.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [Therefore tell them that the Lord Yahweh says that they eat upon the blood]

The term translated as **Therefore** indicates that what follows is a result of what came before. Use a connector in your language that makes this clear. Alternate translation: [So because of what they are saying,]

Yahweh is using **You eat upon the blood** as a common expression of the culture. This could mean: (1) they eat meat that still has the blood in it, which Yahweh’s law forbade. (2) they eat meat at pagan rituals where blood was offered. If this phrase does not have either of these meanings for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You eat meat that has not been drained of its blood]

Yahweh is using **you lift up your eyes to your idols** as a common expression of the culture to mean “you trust in your idols and worship them.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and you look to your idols for help]

Here, **you shed blood** represents “you murder people.” If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [and you kill people]

Yahweh is using the question form for emphasis, to say that they will certainly not possess the land. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [and you will certainly not possess the land!]
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:11.

26.note: Yahweh is using **You have stood upon your sword** as a common expression of the culture. This could mean: (1) they relied on violence to get what they wanted. (2) they kept on committing violence. If this phrase does not have either of these meanings for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [You have depended on violence to get what you want]

Yahweh is referring to having sexual relations with another man’s wife in a polite way by using the phrase **the wife of his neighbor you have defiled**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [each of you has slept with his neighbor’s wife]

27.note: Following the custom of the culture, Yahweh is swearing an oath by his own life, and he is stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). The implied meaning is that the things he describes will certainly happen. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explicitly state the second part of this condition. Alternate translation: [As surely as I live, it will certainly happen that]

Yahweh is using **they will fall by the sword** as a common expression of the culture to mean “they will be killed in battle.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [enemy soldiers will kill them]

27.q: עַל פְּנֵ֣י הַ⁠שָּׂדֶ֔ה לַ⁠חַיָּ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖י⁠ו לְ⁠אָכְל֑⁠וֹ
27.note: The implication is that Yahweh will allow wild animals to devour the people who are out in the open country. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I will allow the wild animals to devour anyone who is in the open country]
The pronoun **him** refers to anyone who is out in the open country. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [I will give anyone who is there]
See how you translated **on the face of the field** in 32:4.

Yahweh is not referring to a specific **living thing**. He means wild animals in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [to the wild animals]

28.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:14.

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **strength** that is characterized by **pride**. He means the strength that the people of the land were proud of. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [the strength that she was proud of]

Yahweh is using **the mountains of Israel** to represent the whole land of Israel. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression from your culture or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the whole land of Israel will be desolate]

This could mean: (1) what follows is the result of the mountains becoming desolate, so that no one passes through them. (2) what follows is the reason for what came before, that the mountains will be desolate because no one passes through them. Use a connector in your language that makes the relationship clear. Alternate translation: [so that no one will pass through them]

29.note: See how you translated this expression in 6:7.

The pronoun **they** refers to the people who are living in the ruins in the land of Israel, whom Yahweh mentioned in verse 24. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And the people living in the ruins in the land of Israel will know]
See how you translated this phrase in 5:9.
See how you translated the similar expression in 6:14.

30.q: וְ⁠אַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם בְּנֵ֣י עַמְּ⁠ךָ֗ הַ⁠נִּדְבָּרִ֤ים בְּ⁠ךָ֙
30.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **the sons of your people** with the information about what they are doing, so that it forms a complete sentence. Alternate translation: [And you, son of man, the sons of your people are speaking with one another about you]

The implication is that **the walls** and **the entrances of the houses** were public places where people gathered to talk. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [beside the walls and in the entrances of the houses, the public places where people met to talk]

Yahweh is using **a man with his brother** as a common expression of the culture to mean “each person with another person.” If this phrase does not have that meaning for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [each person with another person]

30.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר בֹּֽאוּ נָ֣א וְ⁠שִׁמְע֔וּ מָ֣ה הַ⁠דָּבָ֔ר הַ⁠יּוֹצֵ֖א מֵ⁠אֵ֥ת יְהוָֽה
30.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [inviting each other to come and hear what the word is that is going out from Yahweh]
See how you translated the similar expression in [2:1](ta:02).
See how you translated the similar expression in 3:11.

31.q: וְ⁠יָב֣וֹאוּ אֵ֠לֶי⁠ךָ כִּ⁠מְבוֹא עָ֞ם וְ⁠יֵשְׁב֤וּ לְ⁠פָנֶ֨י⁠ךָ֙ עַמִּ֔⁠י
31.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **a people** comes together as a large crowd, so **my people** come to Ezekiel in large numbers. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And my people come to you in large numbers]
See how you translated this expression in [8:1](ta:08).

Yahweh is using **For lusts in their mouth they, they are doing** as a common expression of the culture. This could mean: (1) their talk is full of lustful desires. (2) they speak words of love and devotion with their mouths, but they do not mean them. If this phrase does not have either of these meanings for your readers, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [For their talk is full of lustful desires]

Yahweh is speaking of the desires of the people, **their heart**, as if they were a person who is **going** after **their gain**. He means that they are eager to gain more wealth for themselves. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [they eagerly desire to gain more wealth for themselves]

32.q: וְ⁠הִנְּ⁠ךָ֤ לָ⁠הֶם֙ כְּ⁠שִׁ֣יר עֲגָבִ֔ים יְפֵ֥ה ק֖וֹל וּ⁠מֵטִ֣ב נַגֵּ֑ן
32.note: The point of this comparison is that just as people enjoy **a song of lusts** sung with a beautiful voice and played well, so the people enjoy listening to Ezekiel only as entertainment and do not take his message seriously. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [And behold, they enjoy listening to you only for entertainment, just as they enjoy a love song sung beautifully and played well]

Yahweh is using the term **behold** to focus Ezekiel’s attention on what he is about to say. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [And pay attention: you are]
